problem.title: Students Who Never Improved Their Grades
problem.prompt: You are analyzing a K-12 homework app. The `students` table contains basic student information. The `assignments` table records every assignment submission with its score. The `grade_improvements` table logs when a student improved their score on a resubmission compared to their initial attempt on the same assignment. Write a query to find all students who have submitted at least one assignment but have NEVER improved their grade on any resubmission. Return `student_id`, `student_name`. Order the results by `student_id` ascending.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE students (student_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, grade_level INT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE assignments (assignment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT NOT NULL, assignment_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, score INT NOT NULL, submitted_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE grade_improvements (improvement_id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_id INT NOT NULL, assignment_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, old_score INT NOT NULL, new_score INT NOT NULL, improved_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO students (student_id, student_name, grade_level) VALUES (101, 'Alice Chen', 7), (102, 'Bob Martinez', 8), (103, 'Carol White', 7), (104, 'David Kim', 9), (105, 'Emma Brown', 8); INSERT INTO assignments (assignment_id, student_id, assignment_name, score, submitted_at) VALUES (1, 101, 'Math Quiz 1', 75, '2024-01-10 10:00:00'), (2, 101, 'Math Quiz 1', 85, '2024-01-12 14:00:00'), (3, 102, 'Science Lab', 60, '2024-01-11 09:00:00'), (4, 103, 'History Essay', 80, '2024-01-13 11:00:00'), (5, 104, 'Math Quiz 1', 70, '2024-01-10 10:30:00'), (6, 105, 'Science Lab', 90, '2024-01-14 15:00:00'); INSERT INTO grade_improvements (improvement_id, student_id, assignment_name, old_score, new_score, improved_at) VALUES (1, 101, 'Math Quiz 1', 75, 85, '2024-01-12 14:00:00'), (2, 104, 'Math Quiz 1', 70, 78, '2024-01-15 16:00:00');

composite_moves: anti-join using NOT EXISTS to exclude students present in grade_improvements
join students with assignments to ensure at least one submission

hints: Think about which students appear in one table but not in another.
Use NOT EXISTS to filter out students who have any record in the grade_improvements table.
Join students with assignments to ensure they have submitted work, then exclude those with improvements.
problem.answer_key: SELECT DISTINCT s.student_id, s.student_name FROM students s JOIN assignments a ON s.student_id = a.student_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM grade_improvements gi WHERE gi.student_id = s.student_id) ORDER BY s.student_id;

_meta.scenario: a K-12 homework app tracking assignment turn-in and grade improvement

user_solution:
/*
You are analyzing a K-12 homework app.
The `students` table contains basic student information.
The `assignments` table records every assignment submission with its score.
The `grade_improvements` table logs when a student improved their score on a resubmission 

Write a query:
- Find all students who have submitted at least one assignment but have NEVER improved their grade on any resubmission.

Return `student_id`, `student_name`.
Order the results by `student_id` ascending.

OUTPUT
student_id,
student_name

IN assignments AND NOT IN grade_improvements
*/
SELECT
    student_id,
    student_name
FROM students AS s
    WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM assignments AS a WHERE s.student_id = a.student_id)
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM grade_improvements AS g WHERE g.student_id = s.student_id)
ORDER BY 1;
